modelingNotes: Camp North End: the gabled shed by The Crossroad — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-cne-crossroad-shed.ts

A small one-storey outbuilding of the Army depot on the east side of the campus, where The Crossroad meets the railway: a gabled hall with a lower lean-to along its east side, under a pale metal roof. Its name and use are not recorded; OSM gives it the address 1836 Statesville Avenue.

Evidence: - OSM: way/324608641 (height 6) and its parts way/835850905 (gabled, height 6, roof height 2) and way/835850906 (skillion, height 4, roof height 1). - Lidar, USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016, 0.5 m (measured, NAVD88): ground about 226.5 round it (y = 0); the ridge 233.0 (6.5 m) running along the hall's length; the west eaves 231.6 (5.1 m); the east slope falling to 231.3 (4.8 m) at the lean-to, which falls on to 230.4 (3.9 m) at its outer wall. - Mecklenburg County tax parcel 07903101 (CAMP LANDOWNER LP): improvements dated 1943 and 1987; which is this building's is not recorded. - USGS NAIP orthophoto (public domain): the pale grey metal roof, the plan.

No licensed photo was found (Commons, Openverse, Mapillary). The brick walls (the campus brick), the windows and the door are invented. Built because the lead's list named it (298 m², at the survey's size limit).
Frame: the building's own grid; x along bearing 121.8°, y along 31.8°; placement bearing 31.8. The origin is the outline's centroid, lng −80.8305513, lat 35.2480828.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-cne-crossroad-shed", model "clt-cne-crossroad-shed"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-cne-crossroad-shed.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
